title: The Interview Question That Makes You Stand Out (Most People Don’t Ask It)
description:
In this video, I reveal one knockout interview question that instantly sets you apart from other candidates — plus several gold-standard follow-up questions that hiring managers love. Ask these, and you’ll leave a lasting impression that can help land the offer!

Whether you’re preparing for your next interview or want to stand out in today’s competitive job market, these questions will take you from just another candidate to the top pick fast!

 What you’ll learn:

The exact question hiring managers remember

Powerful follow-ups to show insight and confidence

How to leave a positive, lasting impression

If you want more interview tips, job search strategies, and career hacks, make sure to watch until the end and check out my other videos for insider advice!

transcript: the number one question that can literally turn your interview into an offer. And here's the thing, almost no one asks it. If you're not ending your interview with this, you are missing your mic dra moment. Hi friends, I'm Kate Kersner, career strategist, resume writer, and founder of Kushner Careers, where I get to help clients get hired faster. If we haven't met yet, I'm basically your career obsessed besty and wingwoman who wants to see you win. Let's talk about the final question moment. The one that can make or break the interview. When the interviewer says, "So, do you have any questions for us?" Most people freeze at this moment, but this is your chance to flip the script. You get to shift from candidate to collaborator, someone who's already thinking like part of the team. Start with a few smart strategic questions that show depth. Now, stick around to the end for the mic drop question. But first, I'm going to start with the four categories of questions we want to be thinking about. First is company goals and impact. Here's an example question. What are the company's main goals for the year and how does this position contribute to them? [music] This instantly positions you as someone who thinks big picture, not just about what you'll do, but how you'll add value. The second thing is asking about success metrics. For example, how do you measure success at the [music] 30, 60, and 90day marks? You're showing them your results driven and already planning to hit the ground running. The third is the top performer traits. What do you see in candidates who have been most successful in this role? This gives you a window into what they value most, so you can mirror those traits during the rest of your conversation. And in your thank you note, more about that in a future video. So don't forget to like and subscribe. The fourth one is pain points and solutions. A question would be, what are some of the biggest challenges the team is facing right now and how could this role help solve them immediately? This question does two things. It shows empathy and business awareness and it sets you up beautifully for the final question that seals the deal and it's coming up right now. Here it is the heavyhitting question that gets you the offer. Now, you do this in two simple steps. One, you want to reflect something you heard the recruiter say earlier in the conversation. Maybe a goal, painoint, or challenge. An example would be, "I heard you mentioned the company is working to streamline on boarding for your remote employees." Step two, connect your skills to that need. And then ask, "Here's how I'd approach that based on my experience. Is this how you picture someone succeeding in this role?" Here's an example of the whole question. I heard you say that it has been a challenge to streamline onboarding for your remote employees [music] and improving this is one of your strategic goals. In my last role, I cut on boarding time by 60% by automating global mobility workflows and standardizing processes across multiple regions. Is that how you see me contributing to the team? Or could these skills help solve these pain points? Boom. This one question shows active listening, insight, and confidence. You're not just answering their question. You're demonstrating how you'll show up as a problem solver on day one. It also has them actively talking about you as the candidate, which is very powerful. Now, that's the moment where the interviewer starts picturing you in the role. Next time you're prepping for an interview, remember it's not just about what you say, it's about what you ask. If this helps you, like, subscribe, check me out at pushnercareers.com for even more interview tips and career coaching goodness. And remember, you've got this. You're not just answering their questions. You're showing them they've already found the perfect candidate for the role.
